title: Spraycans to Riches: David Choe
summary: An anonymous narrated retrospective compresses Choe's Koreatown graffiti, art school, commercial work, Slow Jams, Facebook murals and stock, Tokyo jail, gambling, Thumbs Up!, wealth and later practice into a rags-to-riches story. It is retained as a secondary narrative and fact-check queue, not canonical biography: edition/date conflicts, medical causality, award, wealth, gambling, private-residence and motive claims remain attributed or disputed.

quality.assessment: Complete chronological read. Obvious ASR damage is repaired in a separate fixture; no idea is removed. The source is single-narrator but supplies no authenticated line-level identity.

speaker_policy: Treat as one anonymous NARRATOR stream. The channel name does not prove legal identity; publish zero named turns pending provenance and held-out acoustic validation.
places: California College of Arts and Crafts / CCA

connections.relationship: The overview demonstrates how a complex archive becomes one frictionless rags-to-riches plot.
Graffiti is presented as origin story, but exact crews, dates and works need primary evidence.
A damaged interview citation shows why quotations need retrievable originals.
Historic institution naming and attendance dates require school or direct-source confirmation.
Adult-magazine names are potential credit leads, not complete bibliography.
The source collapses precursor, edition and Xeric chronology that object evidence must separate.
Two commissions, compensation terms and motives need dated primary records.
The narrated date conflicts with contemporary KQED evidence and must remain disputed.
Gambling is used as character engine, while amounts and diagnosis remain unverified.
Freight hopping and hitchhiking are romanticized without participant, legal or safety context.
The overview blurs project titles, run taxonomy and production chronology.
IPO-era press estimates are not audited net worth or current value.
The scavenger hunt is a useful lead only after a dated primary source is found.
Temporal proximity between eating and diagnosis does not establish diabetes causation.
Official award databases must replace the narrator's ambiguous Emmy claim.
A historic apartment claim should not become a refreshed location trail.
Wealth at the end of a story does not make dangerous travel universally accessible or wise.
A public-access thesis can inform curation without repeating unsupported pricing claims.

source_notes.claim: The quotation comes from a 2003 `Jaime Wright` interview.
source_notes.assessment: Citation is caption-damaged and unresolved; locate the original before quoting or naming the interviewer.

source_notes.claim: Choe attended California College of Arts for one year in 1995.
source_notes.assessment: Verify the institution's historical name, dates and duration from a primary biography or school record.

source_notes.claim: Slow Jams was self-published in 1996 and received a $5,000 grant in 1999.
source_notes.assessment: Conflicts with surviving edition evidence; separate precursor mini-comic, Xeric cycle and supported edition.

source_notes.claim: The first Facebook mural commission occurred in 2005 on the stated terms.
source_notes.assessment: Verify date, office, intermediary and compensation from Facebook/Choe primary material.

source_notes.claim: The Tokyo arrest happened later in 2005.
source_notes.assessment: Conflicts with contemporary KQED chronology indicating an earlier event; keep disputed until primary records settle it.

source_notes.claim: Casinos allowed wagers of $250,000 per hand.
source_notes.assessment: Highly specific financial/operational claim requires direct attributable evidence; do not repeat as fact.

source_notes.claim: Thumbs Up! ran three seasons and ended in 2010.
source_notes.assessment: Verify against official VICE releases and distinguish original run, later seasons, compilations and archive reposts.

source_notes.claim: Facebook stock made Choe worth $200–500 million.
source_notes.assessment: Historic press estimate, not audited holdings, liquidity, tax treatment or current net worth.
Unsupported medical causality; preserve only as narrator claim and explicitly reject as health guidance.
Likely false or category/credit confusion; require official award records and exact show/category/recipient.

source_notes.claim: Choe turns down huge offers and sells at fair prices.
source_notes.assessment: Subjective current business claim; require direct dated evidence and define the market comparison.
